channel.title: BBC News | UK
channel.description: Updated every minute of every day

item.title: Tories 'must change or face slaughter'
item.description: Tory chairman Theresa May tells her party conference that they must change or face their third crushing election defeat in a row.

item.title: DUP to pull out of executive
item.description: The Democratic Unionist Party is to withdraw from the power-sharing executive at Stormont¸ following allegations of IRA intelligence gathering.

item.title: Sunderland sack Reid
item.description: Peter Reid has been dismissed by Sunderland after their poor start to the Premiership season.

item.title: Shipman suspicions 'drove me mad'
item.description: The woman who triggered the downfall of serial killer Harold Shipman says she felt she was "going mad" over her suspicions of the GP.

item.title: Queen 'treasures' Canadian role
item.description: In a powerful speech as part of her Golden Jubilee tour in Vancouver¸ the Queen underlines her place in Canadian history.

item.title: Blunkett accused of asylum panic
item.description: Plans to push through new measures to make the UK less attractive to fake asylum seekers spark fury in the House of Lords.

item.title: Ian Brady seeks public hearing
item.description: The Moors murderer Ian Brady wants a public hearing to determine whether he should still be detained in a mental institution.

item.title: Many cars offer poor whiplash protection
item.description: The first survey of its kind finds a quarter of cars do not offer enough protection against whiplash injuries.

item.title: Borders closed to stop England hooligans
item.description: Austria and the Czech Republic are refusing entry to any known hooligans to prevent them getting to the Euro 2004 qualifier against Slovakia.

item.title: Archer diary tells of prison life
item.description: Jeffrey Archer shares intimate details of his first taste of prison life in his controversial diary which is being serialised in a national newspaper.

item.title: Shayler 'state secrets' trial begins
item.description: Renegade MI5 agent David Shayler begins his trial at London's Old Bailey for allegedly disclosing state secrets in 1997.

item.title: When death came before dishonour
item.description: As a former kamikaze pilot meets British war veterans BBC News Online investigates what lay behind the self-sacrifice.

item.title: Do MPs answer their e-mails?
item.description: How good are MPs at answering e-mails and faxes from their constituents? A survey suggests that some are better than others.

item.title: Hidden tales of the black home front
item.description: Why don't the history books write about black Britons' war effort? BBC News Online's meets one historian who has unearthed their stories.

item.title: Part one of Archer's diary
item.description: The focus in the Daily Mail is on Archer's jail book and in the other papers on the first day of the Tory party conference.
